evidence.velocity_vs_rigour: you'll define analytics engineering standards and best practices across modelling, testing, documentation and governance
evidence.velocity_vs_rigour_explanation: Responsibilities repeatedly emphasize standards, testing, documentation, and governance with no velocity/speed language present, placing this at rigour.
evidence.domain_risk: At Eftsure, we're on a mission to protect businesses from payment fraud and cyber risk.
evidence.domain_risk_explanation: Eftsure is a payment-fraud-prevention company, and while this specific role focuses on internal analytics rather than the fraud-detection product itself, the domain is inherently fraud/financial-risk-related, placing this at high given the company's core mission and the emphasis on trusted, business-ready data foundations.
evidence.data_team_maturity_explanation: The role is described as taking ownership of an existing analytics engineering capability and 'shaping the future' of the data platform, with existing silver/gold medallion layers and semantic layers already in place, indicating a growing but not yet fully mature function that's actively scaling globally.
evidence.jd_authorship: Working across our silver and gold layers, you'll create clean, reliable and well-documented data assets that become the foundation for reporting, analytics and decision-making.
evidence.jd_authorship_explanation: Responsibilities name precise technical scope (medallion architecture, semantic layer design, dbt production experience, Snowflake/ClickHouse) that shows exactly what the role does day to day, written by someone close to the work.
evidence.stakeholder_orientation: You'll work closely with teams across Product, Customer, Finance, Marketing, Operations and Leadership to understand business challenges
evidence.stakeholder_orientation_explanation: Product, Customer, Finance, Marketing, and Operations are all named as roughly equally weighted stakeholder groups with no single function dominating, making this mixed.
evidence.autonomy_level: take ownership of our analytics engineering capability and help shape the future of our data platform
evidence.autonomy_level_explanation: The role explicitly takes ownership of the analytics engineering capability, defines standards, and shapes the data roadmap, all strategic direction-setting language.
evidence.ai_role: Experience leveraging AI-assisted development tools to improve productivity and quality
evidence.ai_role_explanation: The candidate is expected to use AI-assisted development tools to accelerate their own work, the defining signal of ai_user.
evidence.testing_framing: you'll define analytics engineering standards and best practices across modelling, testing, documentation and governance
evidence.testing_framing_explanation: Testing and governance standards are framed as an owned responsibility with explicit ownership language (define, own), not just a tool in a skills list.
evidence.loss_aversion_framing: you'll create clean, reliable and well-documented data assets that become the foundation for reporting, analytics and decision-making
evidence.loss_aversion_framing_explanation: Data reliability and trust are named as ongoing concerns secondary to the ownership/growth framing, without explicit regulatory or compliance language dominating, placing this at moderate.
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix: help shape the future of our data platform... evaluate opportunities, prototype solutions and contribute to the evolution of our data roadmap
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix_explanation: The JD mixes new-build/roadmap-shaping language (shape the future, prototype solutions) with maintain/scale language (maintain scalable data models, raise the engineering bar on existing practices) roughly evenly, making this mixed.
evidence.loss_aversion: you'll create clean, reliable and well-documented data assets — a secondary quality/trust concern, not an explicit dominant compliance risk register despite the fraud-prevention business context.
